name: Quadrantids
note: A strong but very brief shower: the peak lasts only about six hours, so in some years it falls in daylight for any given place. The radiant lies in northern Boötes, near the end of the Big Dipper's handle, and is highest before dawn. It is a northern-hemisphere shower: the radiant barely rises south of the equator. The name comes from an obsolete constellation, Quadrans Muralis.
source: IMO 2027 Meteor Shower Calendar (ed. J. Rendtel, IMO INFO 3-26), Table 5 'Working List of Visual Meteor Showers', https://www.imo.net/files/data/calendar/cal2027.pdf (fetched 2026-11-10); values cross-checked against English Wikipedia 'List of meteor showers' (parent body from Wikipedia).

name: Lyrids
note: A modest April shower with occasional bright meteors, best after midnight. Meteors appear to stream from a point near Vega (strictly just over the border in Hercules). Best from the northern hemisphere; from mid-southern latitudes the radiant is low in the north before dawn.
source: IMO 2027 Meteor Shower Calendar (ed. J. Rendtel, IMO INFO 3-26), Table 5 'Working List of Visual Meteor Showers', https://www.imo.net/files/data/calendar/cal2027.pdf (fetched 2026-11-10); values cross-checked against English Wikipedia 'List of meteor showers' (parent body from Wikipedia).

name: Eta Aquariids
note: Fast meteors made of dust from Halley's Comet. The shower is rich from the southern hemisphere; from mid-northern latitudes the radiant rises shortly before dawn, so expect only around 10 an hour in the last dark hour of the night.
source: IMO 2027 Meteor Shower Calendar (ed. J. Rendtel, IMO INFO 3-26), Table 5 'Working List of Visual Meteor Showers', https://www.imo.net/files/data/calendar/cal2027.pdf (fetched 2026-11-10); values cross-checked against English Wikipedia 'List of meteor showers' (parent body from Wikipedia).

name: Southern Delta Aquariids
parent: Uncertain; probably the comet 96P/Machholz complex (Wikipedia's list gives P/2008 Y12 (SOHO))
note: Faint meteors over a broad late-July peak, better the farther south you are. From mid-northern latitudes the radiant stays low in the south; from the southern hemisphere it climbs high. Watch after midnight under a dark sky.
source: IMO 2027 Meteor Shower Calendar (ed. J. Rendtel, IMO INFO 3-26), Table 5 'Working List of Visual Meteor Showers', https://www.imo.net/files/data/calendar/cal2027.pdf (fetched 2026-11-10); values cross-checked against English Wikipedia 'List of meteor showers' (parent body from Wikipedia).

name: Perseids
note: The favorite shower of the northern year: fast, bright meteors on August nights. Rates climb from late evening until dawn as the radiant in Perseus rises in the northeast. The radiant is so far north that the shower is poor from the southern hemisphere.
source: IMO 2027 Meteor Shower Calendar (ed. J. Rendtel, IMO INFO 3-26), Table 5 'Working List of Visual Meteor Showers', https://www.imo.net/files/data/calendar/cal2027.pdf (fetched 2026-11-10); values cross-checked against English Wikipedia 'List of meteor showers' (parent body from Wikipedia).

name: Orionids
note: The October shower from Halley's Comet dust: swift meteors radiating from near Orion's raised club, north of Betelgeuse. Best after midnight, with a broad peak lasting several nights, and visible from both hemispheres.
source: IMO 2027 Meteor Shower Calendar (ed. J. Rendtel, IMO INFO 3-26), Table 5 'Working List of Visual Meteor Showers', https://www.imo.net/files/data/calendar/cal2027.pdf (fetched 2026-11-10); values cross-checked against English Wikipedia 'List of meteor showers' (parent body from Wikipedia).

name: Southern Taurids
note: A weak, long-lasting shower of slow meteors known for occasional bright fireballs. Visible most of the night in October and November, with no sharp peak.
source: IMO 2027 Meteor Shower Calendar (ed. J. Rendtel, IMO INFO 3-26), Table 5 'Working List of Visual Meteor Showers', https://www.imo.net/files/data/calendar/cal2027.pdf (fetched 2026-11-10); values cross-checked against English Wikipedia 'List of meteor showers' (parent body from Wikipedia).

name: Northern Taurids
note: The slightly later twin of the Southern Taurids: few meteors, but slow and sometimes brilliant. The radiant is near the Pleiades and is up all night in November.
source: IMO 2027 Meteor Shower Calendar (ed. J. Rendtel, IMO INFO 3-26), Table 5 'Working List of Visual Meteor Showers', https://www.imo.net/files/data/calendar/cal2027.pdf (fetched 2026-11-10); values cross-checked against English Wikipedia 'List of meteor showers' (parent body from Wikipedia).

name: Leonids
note: The fastest shower meteors, radiating from the Sickle of Leo after midnight. Normally modest, but famous for rare meteor storms in years such as 1833, 1966 and 1999–2002.
source: IMO 2027 Meteor Shower Calendar (ed. J. Rendtel, IMO INFO 3-26), Table 5 'Working List of Visual Meteor Showers', https://www.imo.net/files/data/calendar/cal2027.pdf (fetched 2026-11-10); values cross-checked against English Wikipedia 'List of meteor showers' (parent body from Wikipedia).

name: Geminids
note: Usually the richest shower of the year, with bright, medium-speed meteors. The radiant near Castor is well up by mid-evening, so this is the one major shower you can watch before midnight. Dress warmly.
source: IMO 2027 Meteor Shower Calendar (ed. J. Rendtel, IMO INFO 3-26), Table 5 'Working List of Visual Meteor Showers', https://www.imo.net/files/data/calendar/cal2027.pdf (fetched 2026-11-10); values cross-checked against English Wikipedia 'List of meteor showers' (parent body from Wikipedia).

name: Ursids
note: A minor shower around the December solstice radiating from near Kochab in the Little Dipper's bowl. The radiant never sets from mid-northern latitudes and never rises from the southern hemisphere; rates are low, with rare outbursts.
source: IMO 2027 Meteor Shower Calendar (ed. J. Rendtel, IMO INFO 3-26), Table 5 'Working List of Visual Meteor Showers', https://www.imo.net/files/data/calendar/cal2027.pdf (fetched 2026-11-10); values cross-checked against English Wikipedia 'List of meteor showers' (parent body from Wikipedia).
